extracted.intended_audience: offerors, carriers, packaging designers, and compliance officers handling Class 7 (radioactive) materials
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and technical standards for packaging, labeling, contamination control, storage, and shipment (by road, rail, vessel, and aircraft) of Class 7 (radioactive) materials, including fissile material and uranium hexafluoride. Covers allowable indexes, test procedures, approvals, and administrative submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conveyance limits on the sum of package transport indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for shipments by cargo aircraft only or by seagoing vessel, the sum of transport indices for a non-exclusive use shipment may not exceed 50. Where a consignment is transported under exclusive use, there is no limit on the sum of the transport indices aboard a single conveyance (subject to conditions in the regulation). Provisions for air and vessel shipments are referenced in other sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoints: (1) Non-exclusive conveyance sum TI ≤ 50. (2) Exclusive use — no sum TI limit but paragraphs (b)(2),(b)(3),(b)(4) and (c) must be met. (3) Air shipments governed by §§175.700-175.705. (4) Vessel shipments governed by §§176.700-176.720.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft prohibition for packages exceeding surface radiation or TI limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A package exceeding the maximum surface radiation level or maximum transport index prescribed in paragraph (a) of this section may not be transported by aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to both passenger and cargo aircraft per the referenced paragraph (a) limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contamination control — wipe test method and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-fixed contamination shall be assessed by wiping an area of 300 cm2 with moderate pressure and measuring activity on the wipe; the measured activity divided by area and by wipe efficiency may not exceed the limits in Table 9. Alternatively, other methods of equal or greater efficiency may be used to determine non-fixed contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wipe efficiency: actual efficiency may be used or a default assumed efficiency of 0.10. Sufficient measurements must be taken in the most appropriate locations to yield a representative assessment of non-fixed contamination levels. Table 9 provides the maximum permissible limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 9 — non-fixed external radioactive contamination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 9 specifies maximum permissible limits for non-fixed external radioactive contamination for packages by contaminant category (values given in Bq/cm2, μCi/cm2, dpm/cm2). Example categories: (1) Beta and gamma emitters and low toxicity alpha emitters; (2) All other alpha emitting radionuclides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation states: 'The amount of radioactivity measured on any single wiping material ... may not exceed the limits set forth in Table 9 at any time during transport.' Table lists numeric limits for each category (to be consulted in the regulatory text when applying).

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage during transportation — fissile-labeled packages limits and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of packages and overpacks bearing FISSILE labels stored in any one storage area must be limited so the total sum of criticality safety indices (CSI) in any individual group does not exceed 50. Groups must be stored to maintain spacing of at least 6 m (20 feet) from all other groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storage areas include transit areas, terminal buildings, storerooms, waterfront piers, assembly yards. Vessel storage requirements are described elsewhere (subpart M of part 176).

rubrics_metrics.name: General transportation requirement — secure shipments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each shipment of Class 7 (radioactive) materials must be secured to prevent shifting during normal transportation conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic securement requirement applies to all conveyances to prevent package movement that might compromise package integrity or safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: General transportation requirement — stowage/heat output and surface heat flux limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A package or overpack of Class 7 materials may be carried among packaged general cargo without special stowage if (1) the heat output in watts does not exceed 0.1 times the minimum package dimension in centimeters; or (2) the average surface heat flux does not exceed 15 watts per square meter and surrounding cargo is not in sacks or bags that would impede air circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these conditions are not met, special stowage provisions (or other exceptions) may apply per §§174.81, 176.83, 177.848 or the Competent Authority certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passenger compartment restrictions and passenger aircraft limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages bearing labels prescribed in §172.403 may not be carried in compartments occupied by passengers, except compartments exclusively reserved for couriers accompanying those packages. No person shall offer for transport or transport aboard a passenger-carrying aircraft any single package or overpack with a transport index greater than 3.0. No person shall offer for transport or transport aboard a passenger-carrying aircraft any Class 7 material unless that material is intended for use in, or incident to, research, medical diagnosis or treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional passenger-aircraft limits and procedures are in Part 175; placement on aircraft and other handling requirements are specified in related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpack requirements and transport index limits for overpacks
rubrics_metrics.description: If an overpack is used to consolidate individual packages, the package(s) must comply with packaging, marking, and labeling requirements. The overpack must be labeled per §172.403(h), marked per subpart D of part 172 and §173.25(a), and the transport index of the overpack may not exceed 3.0 for passenger-carrying aircraft shipments or 10.0 for cargo-aircraft shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overpack consolidations do not remove the underlying package obligations — underlying packages must still meet all applicable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile material exceptions (§173.453)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain small quantities or configurations of fissile material are excepted from fissile-subpart requirements, provided conditions are met. Exceptions include: (a) individual package ≤ 2 grams fissile; (b) package ≤ 15 g fissile if at least 200 g solid nonfissile per gram of fissile (with specified exclusions); (c) low concentrations commingled with nonfissile where at least 2000 g nonfissile per gram and no more than 180 g fissile within 360 kg contiguous nonfissile; (d) uranium enriched to ≤1% U-235 with limits on plutonium/U-233 and mass of certain materials; (e) specified uranyl nitrate liquid solutions (≤2% U-235, plutonium/U-233 ≤0.002%, N/U≥2) in at least DOT Type A package; (f) packages containing, individually, total plutonium mass ≤1000 g with not more than 20% by mass being Pu-239/Pu-241.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead, beryllium, graphite, and hydrogenous material enriched in deuterium may be present but are excluded from determining required nonfissile mass. Even excepted packages remain subject to other requirements of the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile material package transportation requirements (§173.457)
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages containing fissile material not excepted under §173.453 must be assigned a criticality safety index (CSI) and a transport index (TI) by the offeror, must satisfy radiation level restrictions of §173.441, and must observe CSI limits for consignment and conveyance (including exclusive-use rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key numeric limits and rules: (c) CSI of any package/overpack for non-exclusive use may not exceed 50 (CSI >50 requires exclusive use). (d) For non-exclusive shipments (except on vessels) total CSI in a freight container/conveyance ≤50. (e) For exclusive use shipments (except on vessels) total CSI in a freight container/conveyance ≤100. (f) Exclusive use shipments must satisfy administrative and radiation requirements of §173.441(b). (g) Storage-in-transit group CSI limit ≤50 with 6 m spacing. Vessel shipment provisions referenced separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing fissile packages with other Class 7 materials (§173.459)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixing of fissile material packages with other types of Class 7 materials in any conveyance or storage location is authorized only if the TI of any single package does not exceed 10, the CSI of any single package does not exceed 50, and the provisions of §§173.441 and 173.457 are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixing authorization thus requires both per-package and overall radiation/CSI compliance with the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for special form Class 7 materials — leakage and leaching assessments (§173.469)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sealed capsule specimens need not undergo the leaching assessment if subjected instead to volumetric leakage assessment tests prescribed in ISO 9978-1992(E). The leaching assessment requires immersion and environmental conditioning steps with specified water pH, conductivity, immersion duration, and post-immersion temperature/humidity exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaching test specifics: immerse specimen 7 days at ambient temperature with sufficient water volume (end free volume ≥10% of sample volume), water initial pH 6-8 and max conductivity 1 mS/m at 20°C; then keep at least 7 days in still air at ≥30°C and relative humidity ≥90%. Alternative ISO tests may substitute where specified. Impact/percussion test exceptions apply for small masses (see next item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact/percussion test exception for small special form materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The impact and percussion tests may be omitted for special form radioactive material if mass < 200 g and the specimen is alternatively subjected to the Class 4 impact test in ISO 2919.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISO 2919 (Sealed Radioactive Sources—Classification) Class 4 impact test may be substituted for the section's impact and percussion tests for small masses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for NRC-approved and foreign-made packages (§§173.471, 173.473)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors of NRC-approved package designs (Type B(U), Type B(M), fissile) must comply with applicable NRC and subchapter requirements in addition to those in this subpart. Offerors of foreign-made packages requiring a Competent Authority Certificate must comply with additional requirements and IAEA TS-R-1 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-made package offerors must also comply with §173.473 and related IAEA certification requirements; NRC-approved packages must meet 10 CFR part 71 requirements plus specified subchapter requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of special form Class 7 materials — QA and pre-shipment actions (§173.476(c)(4)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an original request for a Competent Authority Certificate, evidence of a quality assurance program for design/manufacture/testing/documentation/use/maintenance/inspection of special form material is required, and a description of any proposed pre-shipment actions (e.g., leak testing) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA program should be based on international, national or other standards appropriate to the activities covered; pre-shipment actions should be documented and described in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval requirements for packagings >0.1 kg uranium hexafluoride (§173.477)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each offeror of a package containing more than 0.1 kg of uranium hexafluoride (UF6) must maintain for at least one year a complete safety analysis (including tests) demonstrating compliance with §173.420 and must obtain a U.S. Competent Authority Certificate prior to the first export shipment. Requests must be submitted in writing (triplicate) or via fax/email, received at least 90 days before the requested effective date, and include specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required submission contents: (1) safety analysis report with detailed description of packaging and contents, manufacturing process, tests conducted and results, calculative evidence the package can pass tests or other compliance evidence; (2) for original requests, evidence of a quality assurance program. IAEA Certificate may be used to satisfy some requirements. Electronic/fax/address details provided for submission; requests considered in order received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rail carriage special handling — total TI and CSI limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of packages of Class 7 material that may be transported by rail car or stored at any single location is limited to a total transport index and a total criticality safety index of not more than 50 each, except for exclusive use shipments as described in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rail requirements reference §§173.403, 173.427, 173.441, and 173.457 for exclusive use exceptions and interactions; each shipment of fissile material packages must conform to §§173.457 and 173.459.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft carriage — passenger-carrying aircraft special limitations (§175.700)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may transport in a passenger-carrying aircraft any package required to be labeled RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-II, RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-III or FISSILE unless: (1) for RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-III, TI ≤ 3.0; (2) for FISSILE label, CSI ≤ 3.0; (3) the package is carried on the floor of the cargo compartment or in a freight container; (4) carried in accordance with §§175.701 and 175.703; (5) total sum of TIs of all packages in the aircraft ≤ 50; and (6) total sum of CSIs of all packages in the aircraft ≤ 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are cumulative conditions for carriage on passenger aircraft; related operational procedures are in §§175.701–175.705.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft carriage — cargo aircraft only requirements (§175.702)
rubrics_metrics.description: For cargo aircraft only, no person may transport packages labeled RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-II, RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-III or FISSILE unless either: (1) total transport index for all packages ≤ 50 and total CSI ≤ 50 and package carried per §175.701(a); or (2) total TI > 50 but ≤ 200 and total CSI ≤ 100 (with other carriage conditions met).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cargo-aircraft-only shipments may allow higher aggregate TI and CSI up to specified caps, provided the applicable carriage provisions are satisfied.
